subject: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks

Team —

I pulled together the run-rate gap register for our QBR pack and wanted to surface the three items that materially change our launch readiness for the core product release in early May. Spreadsheet attached (RunRate_Gap_Register_Q2.xlsx) and a short readout PDF. High level: we have a ~22% shortfall in expected token throughput from the serving/runtime integration work and two feature toggles (cache priming and dynamic batching) are lower than expected in end-to-end testing.

Key asks:
- Confirm whether leadership is willing to accept a controlled degraded-throughput launch (with hard throttles and fallback model) vs. delaying the public launch by 2 weeks.
- If we proceed, authorize a prioritized hiring/contractor spend to accelerate the runtime kernel tuning (ask = $75k bridge).
- Decision on gating criteria: I recommend we keep the feature set but ship with a documented performance SLA for first 30 days and schedule a staged ramp.

Notes:
- Risk matrix in tab 3; action owners assigned.
- I expect Harper from KahlCo and Sanjay from Novatech to ask about timing — they’re both in the pilot queue.

Next steps: can we do a quick 30-minute sync at 11:00 to lock the decision?

Thanks,

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RunRate_Gap_Register_Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet), QBR_mini-readout_v2.pdf (slides)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks

Thanks Laura — good, clear summary. I reviewed the spreadsheet and the gap math looks right. A couple quick clarifying Qs before the 11:00 sync:

1) The 22% shortfall — how much of that is runway recoverable by config changes (batching, cache priming) vs. kernel-level work that needs external contractor help? Please quantify in expected % recovered under the two scenarios.
2) If we opt to ship degraded and throttle, do we have a solid customer-communication plan and rollback plan? Monica, can you confirm CS and account teams are prepared for that messaging?

My inclination: prefer to avoid a public delay unless it materially impacts the pilot customers. If the pilots are OK with a staged ramp and we can guarantee rollback/fallback model, we can proceed. That said, I’m open to approving the $75k bridge if the kernel work is expected to close >60% of the delta within 7 days.

Put these on the 11:00 agenda — and bring a one-slide plan that maps mitigation -> expected delta recovered -> owner.

Vivek

Subject: Re: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 09:45 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Laura — good, clear summary. I reviewed the spreadsheet and the gap math looks right. A couple quick clarifying Qs before the 11:00 sync:
> 
> 1) The 22% shortfall — how much of that is runway recoverable by config changes (batching, cache priming) vs. kernel-level work that needs external contractor help? Please quantify in expected % recovered under the two scenarios.
> 2) If we opt to ship degraded and throttle, do we have a solid customer-communication plan and rollback plan? Monica, can you confirm CS and account teams are prepared for that messaging?

I've looped in Harper since KahlCo is in pilot and will likely request a firm timeline. Short answers:
- Config-level changes: estimated recoverable = 12-15% (batching + cache priming + tuning defaults).
- Kernel-level work: estimated recoverable = 10-12% in short term (7 day focused effort with contractor).

CS/account readiness: yes, we have a drafted message and rollback FAQ; I can get it into a shared folder before EOD. If we go degraded-live, I recommend the staged ramp: open signups to internal users and closed pilot customers only for 7 days.

Granting the contractor budget is reasonable to me if we get the >60% closure estimate that Vivek mentioned — we should also require milestone checkpoints (3 days, 7 days).

Thanks — I’ll bring the comms slide and rollout plan to the 11:00.

Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QBR_mini-readout_v2.pdf (slides)
From: Harper Mills <harper@kahlco.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks

Hi team — appreciate the transparency and the clear asks. For KahlCo the pilot timeline is important: we can accept a staged ramp if the pilot SLA is preserved and we have a firm date for broader rollout in the event the contractor work is successful. Two asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the fallback model (which model/variant you’ll route to and expected latency impact)?
2) If there’s a 2-week delay, what is the escalation path and credits/compensation policy?

We are available for a short call this afternoon if needed.

—Harper
Harper Mills
Head of AI Integrations, KahlCo
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Harper Mills <harper@kahlco.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novatech.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 readiness: run-rate gaps, proposed mitigations & decision asks

Thanks everyone for the fast replies and for joining the 11:00. Quick decisions and next steps from the sync: 

- We will proceed with a staged public launch (closed pilot + internal ramp) on May 5th with hard throttles and documented SLA for pilot customers.
- Approved $75k contractor bridge on the condition of a 3-day checkpoint that shows >=40% of the gap closed and a 7-day checkpoint target of >=60%. If the 3-day checkpoint fails we will pause the public ramp and re-evaluate.
- Monica: push the CS/account FAQ to the shared Drive folder by EOD and coordinate a short pilot notification template for Harper and Sanjay.
- Karthik & runtime eng: owner for contractor hiring and milestone coordination; please post updates to JIRA INF-9142.

I’ll capture these items into the QBR pack and include a single-slide decision log. Thanks for moving quickly — we can refine the ramp calendar during the prep meeting tomorrow.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Operating Officer
Redwood Inference
